title: Algebraic Kuga–Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus
main_claim: For every projective complex K3 surface S whose transcendental quadratic space embeds rationally and isometrically into U_Q^2 ⊥ <-1>^4 (in particular every ample P-polarized K3 with P = U ⊕ D8(-1) ⊕ D4(-1), Picard jumps included), the exact standard even-Clifford Kuga–Satake tensor is induced by an algebraic cycle. Rational HC and GHC therefore hold in every degree of every self-power S^m. Separately (Thm 1.1), algebraicity of one exact standard tensor implies HC and GHC for all self-powers of any projective K3.

issues.description: The proof says the ambiguity in splitting the truncation triangle lies in an Ext^{j-i} group. The ambiguity actually lies in Hom(tau_{>i}, tau_{<=i}), which is a negative-degree Ext for i<j. That group also vanishes, so the uniqueness claim still holds. This is a mis-stated degree, not a gap.
issues.evidence: For two distinct nonzero even degrees i<j, the obstruction ... lies in an Ext^{j-i+1} group, and the ambiguity lies in an Ext^{j-i} group.

coverage:
I read and checked most of the 5391-line LaTeX source (build/paper.tex). The steps below were checked for logic and, where possible, recomputed.

Section 2 (exact tensor to HC/GHC):
- Clifford PBW injectivity of F_k, the adjoint/Cayley-Hamilton left inverse R_k, and codimension and degree bookkeeping.
- Support-dimension count giving coniveau d-c.
- Real-case volume tensors and eigenprojectors, CM norm-one span, and first-fundamental-theorem assembly.
- Highest-weight carrier lemmas (Hodge level 2*lambda_1, Galois width transport) and the converse inclusion via Deligne.

Section 3 (geometry and lattice):
- Double-cover numerics: g(D')=9, quotient genus 5, e(Y)=40, p_g=2, b2=38, signatures (5,33), (3,19), (2,14), (2,6).
- Sign split 8/8 at the 2-torsion points.
- Determinant and Hasse-invariant computation giving U ≅ V_P.
- Lattice lemma (discriminant forms of D8, D4, U(2)).

Period map (Prop geom:period):
- Log-tangent identification and h^1(E)=6.
- Restriction sequence to the theta curve, rank-3 perturbation A', and the residue pairing (=4) giving invertibility of the period differential.
- Hodge group SO via countably many Hodge loci.

Section 4 (domination by curves):
- Coherent half-sum torsor, signed-relation exclusions, deg F=8, even pullback F^*D=2E by the multiplicity count, and the étale lift to X.

Section 5 (K3 realization):
- Nikulin overlattice reduction, local monodromies (exchanged pair, plus/minus fixed points, -id at infinity).
- Period-stack/Weyl kernel and descent.
- Hodge-line degree 1 on the P^1_u model, so deg(K_C ⊗ lambda) = -1, giving uniruledness via BDPP.

Section 6 (two-substitution comparison):
- Global invariant cycle lift, uniruled H^3 splitting, Hilbert-stratum spreading.
- Cylinder identity t(d)d = -4, vanishing of the cylinder class on threefold fibers, Leray H^1-term functoriality, Thom/coefficient Gysin.
- Localization, strictness and semisimplicity exclusion of the boundary error via Hom(U_b, H_F) = 0.

Section 7 (half-spin spanning):
- Effective weight-one constituents are trivial or half-spin.
- S+⊗S- ⊇ U with multiplicity 1, and dim Hom = 128.
- Spanning of both orientations and the algebraic realization with the sign of the flip.

Sections 8-9 (transfer and specialization):
- Proper-parameter lemma, rational density, the seed argument, compression identity (p⊗b)ι = ι_{pji}, the R_r right-factor change, and the Witt/Buskin transfer.

Read only lightly: the Hilbert-scheme/moduli corollary (de Cataldo–Migliorini, Bülles transfer) and some of the routine charts in Lemma geom:genericity.
